Here are seven tiny upgrades that compound over time, each with one action you can start today:

- Sleep: Set a consistent “lights-out” alarm 8–8.5 hours before wake time. Treat it like an unbreakable meeting.
- Focus: Work in 50/10 blocks. During the 50, put your phone in another room; during the 10, move your body and glance at sunlight.
- Learning: Create a capture system with three buckets: Ideas, Questions, Highlights. Review once weekly and turn the best into one small experiment.
- Fitness: Attach 10 minutes of strength to an existing habit (e.g., after coffee). Rotate push, pull, legs, core. Consistency beats intensity.
- Nutrition: Eat protein-forward at the first meal (20–30g). It steadies appetite and makes better choices easier later.
- Finances: Automate a tiny “wealth tax to yourself” (e.g., 1–5%) into an index fund or high‑yield savings every payday. Increase by 1% each quarter.
- Relationships: Send one “gratitude ping” daily: a two-sentence text to someone specific about something specific.

If you want, pick one area and I’ll turn it into a 2‑week micro-plan.

turns.speaker: A
turns.content_clean:
Awesome—let’s do Focus. Here’s a 2‑week micro‑plan to install 50/10 blocks that actually stick.

Goal by Day 14
- Default work rhythm: 3–4 x 50/10 blocks on priority work, phone in another room, quick sunlight + movement in breaks.
- Track: deep-work minutes, distraction count, and one “win” per day.

Quick setup (15 minutes today)
- Pick a phone drop spot in another room + charger there.
- Install a blocker: Freedom/Cold Turkey/Screen Time to auto-block socials/email during blocks.
- Create a “Block Kit”: water, notepad for intruding thoughts, headphones, single task list.
- Define your “start ritual” (60 seconds): close everything, open only the task, set timer, put phone away.
- Define your “break ritual” (10 minutes): stand, 2-minute walk or mobility, 30–60 seconds sunlight at a window/outside, sip water, quick stretch. No phone until minute 9–10.

Week 1: Build the groove
- Day 1–2: 1 block/day
  - Pick one clear task. Do start ritual. After: note deep-work minutes and one distraction you’ll remove tomorrow.
- Day 3–4: 2 back-to-back morning blocks
  - Use the notepad to park any “I should check…” thoughts.
- Day 5: 2 afternoon blocks (practice doing this when energy is lower)
- Day 6: 3 blocks total (2 AM, 1 PM)
- Day 7: Light day + Review
  - Optional 1 block. Review: average blocks/day, biggest derailers, best time of day. Tweak environment (e.g., move Slack to a separate desktop, pre-download docs).

Week 2: Volume + resilience
- Day 8–9: 3 blocks/day
  - Batch similar tasks per block (writing, analysis, coding, design).
  - End-of-day 5-minute plan for tomorrow’s first block task.
- Day 10: 4 blocks split (2 AM, 2 PM)
  - Protect a 90-minute calendar window labeled “Focus: Do Not Book.”
- Day 11 (meeting-heavy): Minimum viable focus
  - 1 protected 50/10 in the morning. Use 25/5 micros between meetings. Silence notifications; set email/slack check windows at 10:30 and 3:30.
- Day 12 (deep project): 3–4 blocks on one deliverable
  - Define a concrete milestone (e.g., “draft intro + methods,” “ship v1 deck”).
- Day 13 (stress test): Work in a different environment (library/café) with blockers on. Note what breaks and fix it (earplugs, seated away from door, etc.).
- Day 14: Consolidate
  - Review metrics: average blocks/day, best/worst time, top 3 distractions.
  - Lock your standard weekly template (e.g., Mon–Thu: 3 blocks AM, 1 PM; Fri: 2 blocks + admin).
  - Pre‑commit next two weeks on your calendar.

Rules of engagement
- If a block breaks twice, switch that session to 25/5 Pomodoros and finish the hour.
- Urgent channels: set an auto‑reply “In focused work; I’ll check at [next break time].”
- Only one task open per block. “Finish line” = a tangible sub-outcome (500 words, 10 problems, 1 section refactored).
- Track daily in 3 lines: Blocks completed / Distractions count / One win.

Optional boosters
- Use the Forest or Focus To‑Do timer for commitment pressure.
- Start blocks at the same times daily to remove decision fatigue.
- Pair with 2 minutes of light exposure + a short walk before Block 1 for faster “mind warm-up.”

Here’s a tailored weekly template with exact blocks, tool picks/settings, on-call tweaks, and a Friday plan optimized for fewer meetings. All times ET.

Daily anchors and defaults (Mon–Thu)
- 8:45–9:00 P0 scan + load-in
  - Action: 3–5 min scan for pages/escalations only (Slack: only priority channels; email: only [P0]/[Prod] filters). Update day plan.
  - Status: Slack “Heads-down. Urgent? Call/text.” Auto-reply on email on. Enable Freedom/Screen Time.
- 9:00–9:25 Warm-up + task setup
  - Clarify “one big rock” for the AM deep block. Open needed docs/tabs, write a 3–5 line intent in the ticket/notes. Queue any PRs to review in the afternoon.
- 9:30–10:40 Deep work block A (40/10/20)
  - 9:30–10:10 focus, 10:10–10:20 break, 10:20–10:40 focus
  - Work types: core feature implementation, tricky design decisions, or drafting design docs.
- 10:40–10:50 Slack/email check window #1 (desired)
  - Triage in order: mentions/DMs, team channels, then inbox. Capture follow-ups to your task list.
- 10:50–11:10 Meeting prep / buffer
  - Skim agendas, add bullets/questions. If no meetings, keep coding.
- 11:15–11:30 Daily standup
- 11:30–12:15 Meetings cluster or light collab
  - Common: design syncs, sprint ceremonies, quick reviews.
- 12:15–12:45 Lunch (slide ±15 if meetings run long)
- 12:45–2:00 Post‑lunch dip = reactive/low‑cog work
  - Triage, light PR reviews, small tickets, clarifying comments, 1:1s.
- 2:00–2:30 Collab/overflow
  - Ad‑hoc product syncs, quick design huddles, unblock others.
- 2:30–4:25 Deep work block B (split around your check)
  - 2:30–3:10 focus, 3:10–3:20 break, 3:20–3:30 focus
  - 3:30–3:45 Slack/email check window #2 (desired)
  - 3:45–4:25 focus
  - Work types: high‑leverage PRs, architecture work, finishing AM’s big rock.
- 4:25–4:45 Admin wrap
  - Reply to non-urgent messages, update tickets, capture tomorrow’s top 1–2.
- 4:45–5:15 Review/PRs/design feedback or small fixes
  - Leave your evening self a clean runway; shut down at 5:15 to make 5:30 pickup.

Monday specifics
- Sprint planning (late morning): Reserve 11:30–12:15 for sprint planning (adjust if your team’s slot differs).
- Keep Deep work A 9:30–10:40; if sprint planning starts earlier, shift the 10:40 check to 10:35–10:45 and compress prep.

Tuesday/Thursday
- 7:00–8:00 Light workout
- Start work as usual at 8:45. Consider a slightly longer 9:00–9:30 warm-up if you want extra cooldown time.

Wednesday
- Keep default template. If you have midweek 1:1s, place them 12:45–1:15 or 1:15–1:45.

Friday (fewer meetings; optimized plan)
- 8:45–9:00 P0 scan + set weekly review doc
- 9:00–9:25 Light inbox sweep (only to empty obvious quick wins/approvals)
- 9:30–10:40 Deep work A: wrap one core item or write a design doc section
- 10:40–10:50 Check window #1
- 10:50–11:10 Planning prep: pull metrics, review board, note rollovers
- 11:15–11:30 Standup
- 11:30–12:15 Weekly review
  - What shipped/blocked, top learnings, debt list, PR stats, meeting notes to archive
- 12:15–12:45 Lunch
- 12:45–1:30 Backlog grooming + next‑week targets
  - Slot 1–2 “big rocks,” pre‑draft tickets, identify stakeholders
- 1:30–2:00 Admin sweep
  - Expense reports, calendars, bookings, onboarding reviews, doc cleanups
- 2:30–3:10 Deep work B1: refactor/cleanup or design polish
- 3:10–3:20 Break
- 3:20–3:30 Focus sprint (close loop on B1)
- 3:30–3:45 Check window #2
- 3:45–4:25 Deep work B2: code review batch or learn (paper/talk/prototype)
- 4:25–4:45 Weekly send: post updates, share decisions, thank collaborators
- 4:45–5:15 Set up Monday: top 2, environment ready, calendar sanity check

Tool picks and exact settings
- Freedom (desktop + mobile) or Screen Time (iOS)
  - Work session blocklists: news, social, YouTube, Reddit, App Store, “Discover” pages
  - Schedule: Mon–Thu 9:25–10:50 and 2:25–3:45, plus 3:45–4:30; Fri 9:25–10:50 and 2:25–4:30
  - Allow: PagerDuty/on‑call app, Slack, email
  - Enable Locked Mode during non–on‑call weeks
- Slack
  - Status during deep work: “Heads‑down 9:30–10:40 and 2:30–4:25. Urgent? Call/text.”
  - DND automation: On during those blocks; allow mentions/keywords: your name, “P0,” “prod,” “pagerduty,” team‑name
  - Channel‑specific notifications: mute high‑chatter channels except @mentions
  - Saved replies:
    - “In focus block; I check at 10:45/3:30. Text/call if urgent.”
- Email
  - Auto‑reply (workdays, during focus): “I’m in a focus block and check email at ~10:45 and ~3:30 ET. For urgent issues, please call/text.”
  - VIP list: manager, PM, on‑call alias
  - Filters: star/label [P0], [Prod], [Approval], PR review requests
- Visual timer
  - Time Timer or Flow app: pre‑set 40/10 cycles; chime on breaks only
  - Mac menu‑bar timer: Horo or Be Focused for quick starts
- Body‑double (optional)
  - Focusmate: book 9:30 session on heavy days; 2:30 on slog tasks
- Meeting hygiene
  - Auto‑decline 11:00–2:00 unless critical; propose 12:45–1:15 for quick syncs
  - Hold: “Review lane” daily 4:45–5:15 for PRs/feedback, so others know when to expect reviews

On‑call week adjustments
- Availability
  - Keep phone audio on; set PagerDuty to override DND
  - Do not use Locked Mode in Freedom/Screen Time; allow Slack/Email banners
- Cadence shifts
  - Use 30/10 focus cycles instead of 40/10
  - Add a fast triage pass at 9:55–10:00 and 2:00–2:05
  - Prioritize reactive tasks 12:45–2:30; defer brand‑new deep features unless quiet
- Communication
  - Slack status: “On‑call this week. Faster responses; urgent? Call/text.”
  - Keep AM deep block, but pick a scoped subtask with clean stop points
- Recovery
  - If paged heavily overnight, shrink afternoon deep block and do PRs/docs instead

Context‑switch safeguards
- Before any quick question: write a 1–2 line “next step” note in your editor/ticket to re‑enter faster
- After interruptions: 60‑second reset (scan last 10 lines changed, read your intent note, write the next command)
- Batch PRs: tag PRs requiring leverage; review those in 2:30–4:25 block or 4:45–5:15 lane
- Meeting buffer: keep 10:50–11:10 and 2:00–2:30 free whenever possible

Exact calendar holds to copy

- Standup: Mon–Fri 11:15–11:30

- Review lane: Mon–Thu 4:45–5:15; Fri 4:45–5:15 (weekly send/setup on Fri)

  - ACS 4xx vs 5xx split visible; 5xx rate >0.5% over 5m → warn.

  - Emit tenant_id, idp_id, error_code, timing; avoid raw NameID/Email. If needed, hash email domain with stable salt.

Title: SAML SSO Assertion Processing Hardening — Security Review

1) Overview
- Goal: Harden SAML SSO across signature validation, metadata handling, time and replay protections, and operational controls while maintaining compatibility with major IdPs.
- Scope: ACS endpoint, SAML validator, metadata ingestion service, admin UI, and supporting infra.

2) Architecture summary
- Components: Auth service (validator + ACS), Metadata fetcher/validator, Central replay cache (Redis), Admin UI.
- Data flows:
  - AuthnRequest creation → IdP → SAMLResponse POST to ACS.
  - Metadata fetcher → IdP metadata URL (HTTPS + TLS pinning to entityID) → stored with ETag and last-good snapshot.
- Trust anchors: IdP signing keys from metadata (use="signing" only), validated via chain.

3) Threat model and mitigations
- XML Signature wrapping:
  - Register XML ID attrs for Response, Assertion, SubjectConfirmationData; enforce single Signature per signed object; reference URI must match processed element; whitelisted transforms only.
- Weak/legacy algorithms:
  - Allow RSA-PSS (SHA-256) if supported; else RSA-SHA256; reject SHA-1/DSA at library level.
- Audience/Issuer spoofing:
  - Exact match to SP entityID; Issuer exactly matches metadata entityID.
- Replay attacks:
  - HA replay cache keyed on Response.ID, Assertion.ID, InResponseTo; per-tenant bounded LRU; TTL 8h; clustered store.
- Metadata poisoning or stale keys:
  - HTTPS with TLS validation; entityID pinned to URL expectation; ETag/If-None-Match; backoff; validate NotBefore/NotAfter, chain; ignore encryption keys; support multiple signing certs concurrently; last-good rollback.
- Time-based bypass:
  - Clock skew ±5m; arrival must be ≤2m after NotOnOrAfter; NTP drift monitoring and alerting.
- Destination/ACS abuse:
  - Require exact ACS match when AuthnRequest included URL; else accept only configured default/index; Destination must equal ACS.
- DoS via XML expansion or depth:
  - Disable XXE; cap entity/element/attribute counts, unique IDs, nesting depth, and input size; edge/app POST size limits; gzip disabled for ACS.
- Information disclosure:
  - Never log raw assertions; strip PII; hash NameID opt-in; stable error codes; never echo SAML blobs.
- Key rotation continuity:
  - Multiple signing certs supported; overlapping validity windows; expiry alerts at 14/7/1 days.

4) Compatibility considerations
- Tested IdPs: Okta, ADFS/Azure AD, Google, OneLogin.
- Accept signed Response or signed Assertion; prefer Assertion; per-tenant toggle to require signed Assertion for stricter posture.
- Allow RSA-PSS where supported; otherwise RSA-SHA256 ensures broad compatibility.

5) Validation logic (high level)
- Parse with safe XML settings; enforce size/depth/ID caps.
- Determine signed object; verify single Signature; validate transforms and digest; ensure Reference URI == element ID; validate cert against metadata keys.
- Validate Issuer, AudienceRestriction, Conditions, SubjectConfirmationData (time and recipient), Destination, InResponseTo.
- Check replay cache for Response.ID, Assertion.ID, InResponseTo; write on success.
- Extract attributes; do not log raw values.

6) Operational controls and monitoring
- Metrics: ACS request rate, signature validation failures (code by reason), cache hit/miss/evictions, metadata fetch success/age, cert expiry days, NTP drift, rate-limit throttles.
- Alerts:
  - Cert expiry at 14/7/1 days.
  - NTP drift > 200 ms.
  - Spike in signature failures or XML limit rejections.
  - Replay cache latency > 5 ms p99 or error rate > 1%.
- Dashboards: ACS health, metadata freshness, cache health, error codes.

7) Testing plan
- Golden paths across Okta/ADFS/Azure AD/Google/OneLogin with signed Assertion and signed Response variants.
- Negative/adversarial:
  - Duplicate IDs, duplicate Assertions/Responses.
  - Two Signatures with different refs.
  - Unknown/banned transforms, XPath/XSLT.
  - Wrapping via Additional Assertions or altered IDs.
  - Huge Attributes, malicious namespaces, deep nesting.
  - Compressed POST rejection.
  - Wrong Audience/Issuer, wrong Destination/ACS, expired/not-yet-valid Conditions, skew edges.
  - RSA-PSS vs RSA-SHA256; SHA-1/DSA rejection.
- CI integration and nightly runs; fixtures stored securely; PII-free artifacts.

8) Residual risks and rollbacks
- IdPs with misconfigured metadata or mismatched entityIDs may need coordination; provide per-tenant toggles and staged rollout.
- If metadata fetch fails, use last-good snapshot with TTL and alert.
- Feature flags:
  - requireSignedAssertion (per-tenant).
  - RSA-PSS enablement (global/tenant).
  - Strict Destination/ACS enforcement (global default on).
- Rollback: toggle stricter checks off per-tenant while engaging IdP owners.

9) Documentation and Admin UX
- Clear guidance on supported algorithms, ACS URLs, Audience, Issuer expectations.
- “Test connection” simulates full validation and returns stable, non-PII errors.

10) References
- SAML Profiles/Bindings/Metadata specs.
- OWASP SAML Security Cheat Sheet.
- XML Signature Best Practices (ENISA/NIST).
- Vendor docs: Okta, Microsoft ADFS/Azure AD, Google, OneLogin.

  - 10 tickets above with owners/estimates and acceptance criteria.
  - Security review doc as a PR in the security-reviews repo.

Script: gather_saml_hardening_context.sh
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# ==========================
# REQUIRED ENV VARS
# ==========================
# Jira
: "${JIRA_EMAIL:?Set JIRA_EMAIL}"
: "${JIRA_API_TOKEN:?Set JIRA_API_TOKEN}"
: "${JIRA_DOMAIN:?Set JIRA_DOMAIN (e.g., your-domain.atlassian.net)}"
: "${JIRA_BOARD_ID:?Set JIRA_BOARD_ID for the SAML team board}"

# Slack
: "${SLACK_TOKEN:?Set SLACK_TOKEN (bot or user token with channels:read)}"

# PagerDuty
: "${PD_API_TOKEN:?Set PD_API_TOKEN}"

# GitHub
: "${GITHUB_ORG:?Set GITHUB_ORG}"
# Space/comma separated list of repos you use. Example:
# export GITHUB_REPOS="security-reviews auth-service admin-ui infra infra-terraform qa-automation"
: "${GITHUB_REPOS:?Set GITHUB_REPOS (space-separated: security-reviews auth-service admin-ui infra/infra-terraform qa-automation)}"

# ==========================
# OPTIONAL ENV VARS
# ==========================
# If you want to auto-check default branches via gh CLI, ensure gh is logged in.
: "${USE_GH_CLI:=1}"       # set to 0 to skip gh CLI and leave defaults as main
# Infra repo to check terraform/modules path. If you have both, set preferred first.
: "${INFRA_CANDIDATES:=infra infra-terraform}"
# If you want to confirm terraform/modules exists via GitHub API (no gh CLI), set a token:
: "${GITHUB_TOKEN:=}"
# Vault checks (optional). Set VAULT_ADDR/VAULT_TOKEN and TENANTS (space-separated) to confirm paths.
: "${VAULT_ADDR:=}"
: "${VAULT_TOKEN:=}"
: "${TENANTS:=}"           # e.g., "acme corp-x staging-demo"

jira_auth="-u ${JIRA_EMAIL}:${JIRA_API_TOKEN}"
slack_auth="-H Authorization: Bearer ${SLACK_TOKEN}"
pd_auth="-H Authorization: Token token=${PD_API_TOKEN}"

jq_sprint_filter='.values[] | select(.name|test("SAML Hardening Sprint")) | "\(.name): \(.id)"'

get_jira_sprints() {
  curl -s ${jira_auth} "https://${JIRA_DOMAIN}/rest/agile/1.0/board/${JIRA_BOARD_ID}/sprint?state=active,future,closed" \
    | jq -r "$jq_sprint_filter" \
    | sort -V || true
}

get_jira_custom_fields() {
  curl -s ${jira_auth} "https://${JIRA_DOMAIN}/rest/api/3/field" \
    | jq -r '.[] | select(.name=="Environment" or .name=="Risk" or .name=="Tracking OKR") | "\(.name): \(.id)"' || true
}

get_slack_channel_id() {
  local name="$1"
  curl -s -X GET ${slack_auth} "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?types=public_channel,private_channel&limit=1000" \
    | jq -r --arg n "$name" '.channels[]? | select(.name==$n) | .id' | head -n1
}

get_pd_service_id() {
  local query="$1"
  curl -s ${pd_auth} -H 'Accept: application/vnd.pagerduty+json;version=2' \
    "https://api.pagerduty.com/services?query=$(printf %s "$query" | sed 's/ /%20/g')" \
    | jq -r --arg q "$query" '.services[] | select(.name|test($q;"i")) | "\(.name): \(.id)"' | head -n1
}

get_repo_default_branch() {
  local repo="$1"
  if [[ "$USE_GH_CLI" == "1" ]] && command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    gh repo view "${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}" --json nameWithOwner,defaultBranchRef -q '"\(.nameWithOwner): \(.defaultBranchRef.name)"' 2>/dev/null || echo ""
  else
    if [[ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN}" ]]; then
      curl -s -H "Authorization: token ${GITHUB_TOKEN}" "https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}" \
        | jq -r '"\(.full_name): \(.default_branch)"' 2>/dev/null || echo ""
    else
      # Fallback: assume main (can be corrected manually)
      echo "${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}: main"
    fi
  fi
}

confirm_infra_modules_path() {
  local repo="$1"
  if [[ "$USE_GH_CLI" == "1" ]] && command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if gh api "repos/${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}/contents/terraform/modules" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}:/terraform/modules"
      return 0
    fi
  elif [[ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN}" ]]; then
    if curl -s -H "Authorization: token ${GITHUB_TOKEN}" \
      "https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}/contents/terraform/modules" | jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}:/terraform/modules"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  return 1
}

vault_confirm_path() {
  local p="$1"
  if [[ -z "${VAULT_ADDR}" || -z "${VAULT_TOKEN}" ]]; then
    echo "UNCONFIRMED"
    return
  fi
  if command -v vault >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    VAULT_ADDR="$VAULT_ADDR" VAULT_TOKEN="$VAULT_TOKEN" vault kv metadata get "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "OK" || echo "MISSING"
  else
    # Best-effort via HTTP API (KVv2 assumed). Strip 'kv/' mount and build URL.
    local mount="${p%%/*}" ; local rest="${p#*/}"
    local path="v1/${mount}/metadata/${rest}"
    curl -s -H "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" "${VAULT_ADDR}/${path}" | jq -e .data >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "OK" || echo "MISSING"
  fi
}

# Collect Jira data
mapfile -t sprint_lines < <(get_jira_sprints)
env_id=$(get_jira_custom_fields | awk -F': ' '/^Environment: /{print $2}')
risk_id=$(get_jira_custom_fields | awk -F': ' '/^Risk: /{print $2}')
okr_id=$(get_jira_custom_fields | awk -F': ' '/^Tracking OKR: /{print $2}')

# Slack IDs
auth_alerts_id=$(get_slack_channel_id "auth-alerts" || true)
oncall_sre_id=$(get_slack_channel_id "oncall-sre" || true)

# PagerDuty
pd_auth_service=$(get_pd_service_id "auth-service" | awk -F': ' '{print $2}')
pd_edge_gateway=$(get_pd_service_id "edge|gateway" | awk -F': ' '{print $2}')
if [[ -z "$pd_edge_gateway" ]]; then
  pd_edge_gateway=$(get_pd_service_id "edge gateway" | awk -F': ' '{print $2}')
fi
pd_redis_cache=$(get_pd_service_id "redis|cache" | awk -F': ' '{print $2}')
if [[ -z "$pd_redis_cache" ]]; then
  pd_redis_cache=$(get_pd_service_id "redis cache" | awk -F': ' '{print $2}')
fi

# GitHub repos and default branches
declare -A repo_defaults
for r in $GITHUB_REPOS; do
  # allow org/repo entries or just repo (assume org if not provided)
  if [[ "$r" == */* ]]; then
    repo="${r#*/}"
  else
    repo="$r"
  fi
  line=$(get_repo_default_branch "$repo")
  if [[ -n "$line" ]]; then
    repo_defaults["$repo"]="${line#*: }"
  else
    repo_defaults["$repo"]="main"
  fi
done

# Infra modules path confirmation
infra_path=""
for candidate in $INFRA_CANDIDATES; do
  if [[ -n "$(confirm_infra_modules_path "$candidate" || true)" ]]; then
    infra_path="$(confirm_infra_modules_path "$candidate")"
    break
  fi
done

# Vault confirmations (optional)
kv_nonprod_meta_status="UNCONFIRMED"
kv_prod_meta_status="UNCONFIRMED"
if [[ -n "$TENANTS" ]]; then
  # If tenants provided, report OK only if all tenant paths exist
  all_ok_np=1; all_ok_p=1
  for t in $TENANTS; do
    s1=$(vault_confirm_path "kv/nonprod/saml/metadata/${t}")
    s2=$(vault_confirm_path "kv/prod/saml/metadata/${t}")
    [[ "$s1" == "OK" ]] || all_ok_np=0
    [[ "$s2" == "OK" ]] || all_ok_p=0
  done
  [[ $all_ok_np -eq 1 ]] && kv_nonprod_meta_status="OK" || kv_nonprod_meta_status="MISSING"
  [[ $all_ok_p  -eq 1 ]] && kv_prod_meta_status="OK"    || kv_prod_meta_status="MISSING"
fi
kv_nonprod_replay_status=$(vault_confirm_path "kv/nonprod/saml/replay/redis")
kv_prod_replay_status=$(vault_confirm_path "kv/prod/saml/replay/redis")

# Output the minimal paste block
echo "Minimal paste block"
echo "- Jira"
echo "  - Sprint IDs"
# Default expected names: SAML Hardening Sprint 1..4
for i in 1 2 3 4; do
  id_line=$(printf "%s\n" "${sprint_lines[@]}" | awk -F': ' -v n="SAML Hardening Sprint ${i}" '$1==n{print $2}' | head -n1)
  if [[ -n "$id_line" ]]; then
    echo "    - SAML Hardening Sprint ${i}: ${id_line}"
  else
    echo "    - SAML Hardening Sprint ${i}: <SPRINT_ID_${i}>"
  fi
done
echo "  - Custom field IDs"
echo "    - Environment: ${env_id:-<customfield_#####>}"
echo "    - Risk: ${risk_id:-<customfield_#####>}"
echo "    - Tracking OKR: ${okr_id:-<customfield_#####>}"
echo "- GitHub repos"
# security-reviews
sr_branch="${repo_defaults[security-reviews]:-main}"
echo "  - ${GITHUB_ORG}/security-reviews: ${GITHUB_ORG}/security-reviews${sr_branch:+ (default branch: ${sr_branch})}"
# auth-service
as_branch="${repo_defaults[auth-service]:-main}"
echo "  - ${GITHUB_ORG}/auth-service: ${GITHUB_ORG}/auth-service${as_branch:+ (default branch: ${as_branch})}"
# admin-ui
ui_branch="${repo_defaults[admin-ui]:-main}"
echo "  - ${GITHUB_ORG}/admin-ui: ${GITHUB_ORG}/admin-ui${ui_branch:+ (default branch: ${ui_branch})}"
# infra / infra-terraform
if [[ -n "$infra_path" ]]; then
  echo "  - ${infra_path%%:*}: ${infra_path%:*} (confirm ${infra_path#*:} path)"
else
  # Fallback: show candidates
  for c in $INFRA_CANDIDATES; do
    echo "  - ${GITHUB_ORG}/${c} or ${GITHUB_ORG}/${c}: ${GITHUB_ORG}/${c} (confirm /terraform/modules path)"
  done
fi
# qa-automation
qa_branch="${repo_defaults[qa-automation]:-main}"
echo "  - ${GITHUB_ORG}/qa-automation: ${GITHUB_ORG}/qa-automation${qa_branch:+ (default branch: ${qa_branch})}"
echo "- Slack"
echo "  - #auth-alerts: ${auth_alerts_id:-<CXXXXXXXX>}"
echo "  - #oncall-sre: ${oncall_sre_id:-<CXXXXXXXX>}"
echo "- PagerDuty"
echo "  - auth-service: ${pd_auth_service:-<PD_SERVICE_OR_ESC_ID>}"
echo "  - edge/gateway: ${pd_edge_gateway:-<PD_SERVICE_OR_ESC_ID>}"
echo "  - redis/cache: ${pd_redis_cache:-<PD_SERVICE_OR_ESC_ID>}"
echo "- Vault and CI"
echo "  - kv/nonprod/saml/metadata/{tenant}: ${kv_nonprod_meta_status:-<CONFIRM>}"
echo "  - kv/prod/saml/metadata/{tenant}: ${kv_prod_meta_status:-<CONFIRM>}"
echo "  - kv/nonprod/saml/replay/redis: ${kv_nonprod_replay_status:-<CONFIRM>}"
echo "  - kv/prod/saml/replay/redis: ${kv_prod_replay_status:-<CONFIRM>}"
echo "  - GitHub OIDC role: saml-hardening-ro"
echo "  - GitHub OIDC auth path: auth/jwt/role/saml-hardening-ro"
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Goal by Day 14
- Default work rhythm: 3–4 x 50/10 blocks on priority work, phone in another room, quick sunlight + movement in breaks.

Quick setup (15 minutes today)
- Pick a phone drop spot in another room + charger there.
- Install a blocker: Freedom/Cold Turkey/Screen Time to auto-block socials/email during blocks.
- Create a “Block Kit”: water, notepad for intruding thoughts, headphones, single task list.
- Define your “start ritual” (60 seconds): close everything, open only the task, set timer, put phone away.
- Define your “break ritual” (10 minutes): stand, 2-minute walk or mobility, 30–60 seconds sunlight at a window/outside, sip water, quick stretch. No phone until minute 9–10.

Week 1: Build the groove

  - Pick one clear task. Do start ritual. After: note deep-work minutes and one distraction you’ll remove tomorrow.
- Day 3–4: 2 back-to-back morning blocks
  - Use the notepad to park any “I should check…” thoughts.
- Day 5: 2 afternoon blocks (practice doing this when energy is lower)
- Day 6: 3 blocks total (2 AM, 1 PM)
- Day 7: Light day + Review
  - Optional 1 block. Review: average blocks/day, biggest derailers, best time of day. Tweak environment (e.g., move Slack to a separate desktop, pre-download docs).

Week 2: Volume + resilience
- Day 8–9: 3 blocks/day
  - Batch similar tasks per block (writing, analysis, coding, design).
  - End-of-day 5-minute plan for tomorrow’s first block task.
- Day 10: 4 blocks split (2 AM, 2 PM)

Title: SAML SSO Assertion Processing Hardening — Security Review

1) Overview
- Goal: Harden SAML SSO across signature validation, metadata handling, time and replay protections, and operational controls while maintaining compatibility with major IdPs.
- Scope: ACS endpoint, SAML validator, metadata ingestion service, admin UI, and supporting infra.

2) Architecture summary
- Components: Auth service (validator + ACS), Metadata fetcher/validator, Central replay cache (Redis), Admin UI.
- Data flows:
  - AuthnRequest creation → IdP → SAMLResponse POST to ACS.
  - Metadata fetcher → IdP metadata URL (HTTPS + TLS pinning to entityID) → stored with ETag and last-good snapshot.
- Trust anchors: IdP signing keys from metadata (use="signing" only), validated via chain.

3) Threat model and mitigations
- XML Signature wrapping:
  - Register XML ID attrs for Response, Assertion, SubjectConfirmationData; enforce single Signature per signed object; reference URI must match processed element; whitelisted transforms only.
- Weak/legacy algorithms:
  - Allow RSA-PSS (SHA-256) if supported; else RSA-SHA256; reject SHA-1/DSA at library level.
- Audience/Issuer spoofing:
  - Exact match to SP entityID; Issuer exactly matches metadata entityID.
- Replay attacks:
  - HA replay cache keyed on Response.ID, Assertion.ID, InResponseTo; per-tenant bounded LRU; TTL 8h; clustered store.
- Metadata poisoning or stale keys:
  - HTTPS with TLS validation; entityID pinned to URL expectation; ETag/If-None-Match; backoff; validate NotBefore/NotAfter, chain; ignore encryption keys; support multiple signing certs concurrently; last-good rollback.
- Time-based bypass:
  - Clock skew ±5m; arrival must be ≤2m after NotOnOrAfter; NTP drift monitoring and alerting.
- Destination/ACS abuse:
  - Require exact ACS match when AuthnRequest included URL; else accept only configured default/index; Destination must equal ACS.
- DoS via XML expansion or depth:
  - Disable XXE; cap entity/element/attribute counts, unique IDs, nesting depth, and input size; edge/app POST size limits; gzip disabled for ACS.
- Information disclosure:
  - Never log raw assertions; strip PII; hash NameID opt-in; stable error codes; never echo SAML blobs.
- Key rotation continuity:
  - Multiple signing certs supported; overlapping validity windows; expiry alerts at 14/7/1 days.

4) Compatibility considerations
- Tested IdPs: Okta, ADFS/Azure AD, Google, OneLogin.
- Accept signed Response or signed Assertion; prefer Assertion; per-tenant toggle to require signed Assertion for stricter posture.
- Allow RSA-PSS where supported; otherwise RSA-SHA256 ensures broad compatibility.

5) Validation logic (high level)
- Parse with safe XML settings; enforce size/depth/ID caps.
- Determine signed object; verify single Signature; validate transforms and digest; ensure Reference URI == element ID; validate cert against metadata keys.
- Validate Issuer, AudienceRestriction, Conditions, SubjectConfirmationData (time and recipient), Destination, InResponseTo.
- Check replay cache for Response.ID, Assertion.ID, InResponseTo; write on success.
- Extract attributes; do not log raw values.

6) Operational controls and monitoring
- Metrics: ACS request rate, signature validation failures (code by reason), cache hit/miss/evictions, metadata fetch success/age, cert expiry days, NTP drift, rate-limit throttles.
- Alerts:
  - Cert expiry at 14/7/1 days.
  - NTP drift > 200 ms.
  - Spike in signature failures or XML limit rejections.
  - Replay cache latency > 5 ms p99 or error rate > 1%.
- Dashboards: ACS health, metadata freshness, cache health, error codes.

7) Testing plan
- Golden paths across Okta/ADFS/Azure AD/Google/OneLogin with signed Assertion and signed Response variants.
- Negative/adversarial:
  - Duplicate IDs, duplicate Assertions/Responses.
  - Two Signatures with different refs.
  - Unknown/banned transforms, XPath/XSLT.
  - Wrapping via Additional Assertions or altered IDs.
  - Huge Attributes, malicious namespaces, deep nesting.
  - Compressed POST rejection.
  - Wrong Audience/Issuer, wrong Destination/ACS, expired/not-yet-valid Conditions, skew edges.
  - RSA-PSS vs RSA-SHA256; SHA-1/DSA rejection.
- CI integration and nightly runs; fixtures stored securely; PII-free artifacts.

8) Residual risks and rollbacks
- IdPs with misconfigured metadata or mismatched entityIDs may need coordination; provide per-tenant toggles and staged rollout.
- If metadata fetch fails, use last-good snapshot with TTL and alert.
- Feature flags:
  - requireSignedAssertion (per-tenant).
  - RSA-PSS enablement (global/tenant).
  - Strict Destination/ACS enforcement (global default on).
- Rollback: toggle stricter checks off per-tenant while engaging IdP owners.

9) Documentation and Admin UX
- Clear guidance on supported algorithms, ACS URLs, Audience, Issuer expectations.
- “Test connection” simulates full validation and returns stable, non-PII errors.

10) References
- SAML Profiles/Bindings/Metadata specs.
- OWASP SAML Security Cheat Sheet.
- XML Signature Best Practices (ENISA/NIST).
- Vendor docs: Okta, Microsoft ADFS/Azure AD, Google, OneLogin.

  - 10 tickets above with owners/estimates and acceptance criteria.
  - Security review doc as a PR in the security-reviews repo.

Script: gather_saml_hardening_context.sh
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# ==========================
# REQUIRED ENV VARS
# ==========================
# Jira
: "${JIRA_EMAIL:?Set JIRA_EMAIL}"
: "${JIRA_API_TOKEN:?Set JIRA_API_TOKEN}"
: "${JIRA_DOMAIN:?Set JIRA_DOMAIN (e.g., your-domain.atlassian.net)}"
: "${JIRA_BOARD_ID:?Set JIRA_BOARD_ID for the SAML team board}"

# Slack
: "${SLACK_TOKEN:?Set SLACK_TOKEN (bot or user token with channels:read)}"

# PagerDuty
: "${PD_API_TOKEN:?Set PD_API_TOKEN}"

# GitHub
: "${GITHUB_ORG:?Set GITHUB_ORG}"
# Space/comma separated list of repos you use. Example:
# export GITHUB_REPOS="security-reviews auth-service admin-ui infra infra-terraform qa-automation"
: "${GITHUB_REPOS:?Set GITHUB_REPOS (space-separated: security-reviews auth-service admin-ui infra/infra-terraform qa-automation)}"

# ==========================
# OPTIONAL ENV VARS
# ==========================
# If you want to auto-check default branches via gh CLI, ensure gh is logged in.
: "${USE_GH_CLI:=1}"       # set to 0 to skip gh CLI and leave defaults as main
# Infra repo to check terraform/modules path. If you have both, set preferred first.
: "${INFRA_CANDIDATES:=infra infra-terraform}"
# If you want to confirm terraform/modules exists via GitHub API (no gh CLI), set a token:
: "${GITHUB_TOKEN:=}"
# Vault checks (optional). Set VAULT_ADDR/VAULT_TOKEN and TENANTS (space-separated) to confirm paths.
: "${VAULT_ADDR:=}"
: "${VAULT_TOKEN:=}"
: "${TENANTS:=}"           # e.g., "acme corp-x staging-demo"

jira_auth="-u ${JIRA_EMAIL}:${JIRA_API_TOKEN}"
slack_auth="-H Authorization: Bearer ${SLACK_TOKEN}"
pd_auth="-H Authorization: Token token=${PD_API_TOKEN}"

jq_sprint_filter='.values[] | select(.name|test("SAML Hardening Sprint")) | "\(.name): \(.id)"'

get_jira_sprints() {
  curl -s ${jira_auth} "https://${JIRA_DOMAIN}/rest/agile/1.0/board/${JIRA_BOARD_ID}/sprint?state=active,future,closed" \
    | jq -r "$jq_sprint_filter" \
    | sort -V || true
}

get_jira_custom_fields() {
  curl -s ${jira_auth} "https://${JIRA_DOMAIN}/rest/api/3/field" \
    | jq -r '.[] | select(.name=="Environment" or .name=="Risk" or .name=="Tracking OKR") | "\(.name): \(.id)"' || true
}

get_slack_channel_id() {
  local name="$1"
  curl -s -X GET ${slack_auth} "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?types=public_channel,private_channel&limit=1000" \
    | jq -r --arg n "$name" '.channels[]? | select(.name==$n) | .id' | head -n1
}

get_pd_service_id() {
  local query="$1"
  curl -s ${pd_auth} -H 'Accept: application/vnd.pagerduty+json;version=2' \
    "https://api.pagerduty.com/services?query=$(printf %s "$query" | sed 's/ /%20/g')" \
    | jq -r --arg q "$query" '.services[] | select(.name|test($q;"i")) | "\(.name): \(.id)"' | head -n1
}

get_repo_default_branch() {
  local repo="$1"
  if [[ "$USE_GH_CLI" == "1" ]] && command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    gh repo view "${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}" --json nameWithOwner,defaultBranchRef -q '"\(.nameWithOwner): \(.defaultBranchRef.name)"' 2>/dev/null || echo ""
  else
    if [[ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN}" ]]; then
      curl -s -H "Authorization: token ${GITHUB_TOKEN}" "https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}" \
        | jq -r '"\(.full_name): \(.default_branch)"' 2>/dev/null || echo ""
    else
      # Fallback: assume main (can be corrected manually)
      echo "${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}: main"
    fi
  fi
}

confirm_infra_modules_path() {
  local repo="$1"
  if [[ "$USE_GH_CLI" == "1" ]] && command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if gh api "repos/${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}/contents/terraform/modules" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}:/terraform/modules"
      return 0
    fi
  elif [[ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN}" ]]; then
    if curl -s -H "Authorization: token ${GITHUB_TOKEN}" \
      "https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}/contents/terraform/modules" | jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "${GITHUB_ORG}/${repo}:/terraform/modules"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  return 1
}

vault_confirm_path() {
  local p="$1"
  if [[ -z "${VAULT_ADDR}" || -z "${VAULT_TOKEN}" ]]; then
    echo "UNCONFIRMED"
    return
  fi
  if command -v vault >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    VAULT_ADDR="$VAULT_ADDR" VAULT_TOKEN="$VAULT_TOKEN" vault kv metadata get "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "OK" || echo "MISSING"
  else
    # Best-effort via HTTP API (KVv2 assumed). Strip 'kv/' mount and build URL.
    local mount="${p%%/*}" ; local rest="${p#*/}"
    local path="v1/${mount}/metadata/${rest}"
    curl -s -H "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" "${VAULT_ADDR}/${path}" | jq -e .data >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "OK" || echo "MISSING"
  fi
}

# Collect Jira data
mapfile -t sprint_lines < <(get_jira_sprints)
env_id=$(get_jira_custom_fields | awk -F': ' '/^Environment: /{print $2}')
risk_id=$(get_jira_custom_fields | awk -F': ' '/^Risk: /{print $2}')
okr_id=$(get_jira_custom_fields | awk -F': ' '/^Tracking OKR: /{print $2}')

# Slack IDs
auth_alerts_id=$(get_slack_channel_id "auth-alerts" || true)
oncall_sre_id=$(get_slack_channel_id "oncall-sre" || true)

# PagerDuty
pd_auth_service=$(get_pd_service_id "auth-service" | awk -F': ' '{print $2}')
pd_edge_gateway=$(get_pd_service_id "edge|gateway" | awk -F': ' '{print $2}')
if [[ -z "$pd_edge_gateway" ]]; then
  pd_edge_gateway=$(get_pd_service_id "edge gateway" | awk -F': ' '{print $2}')
fi
pd_redis_cache=$(get_pd_service_id "redis|cache" | awk -F': ' '{print $2}')
if [[ -z "$pd_redis_cache" ]]; then
  pd_redis_cache=$(get_pd_service_id "redis cache" | awk -F': ' '{print $2}')
fi

# GitHub repos and default branches
declare -A repo_defaults
for r in $GITHUB_REPOS; do
  # allow org/repo entries or just repo (assume org if not provided)
  if [[ "$r" == */* ]]; then
    repo="${r#*/}"
  else
    repo="$r"
  fi
  line=$(get_repo_default_branch "$repo")
  if [[ -n "$line" ]]; then
    repo_defaults["$repo"]="${line#*: }"
  else
    repo_defaults["$repo"]="main"
  fi
done

# Infra modules path confirmation
infra_path=""
for candidate in $INFRA_CANDIDATES; do
  if [[ -n "$(confirm_infra_modules_path "$candidate" || true)" ]]; then
    infra_path="$(confirm_infra_modules_path "$candidate")"
    break
  fi
done

# Vault confirmations (optional)
kv_nonprod_meta_status="UNCONFIRMED"
kv_prod_meta_status="UNCONFIRMED"
if [[ -n "$TENANTS" ]]; then
  # If tenants provided, report OK only if all tenant paths exist
  all_ok_np=1; all_ok_p=1
  for t in $TENANTS; do
    s1=$(vault_confirm_path "kv/nonprod/saml/metadata/${t}")
    s2=$(vault_confirm_path "kv/prod/saml/metadata/${t}")
    [[ "$s1" == "OK" ]] || all_ok_np=0
    [[ "$s2" == "OK" ]] || all_ok_p=0
  done
  [[ $all_ok_np -eq 1 ]] && kv_nonprod_meta_status="OK" || kv_nonprod_meta_status="MISSING"
  [[ $all_ok_p  -eq 1 ]] && kv_prod_meta_status="OK"    || kv_prod_meta_status="MISSING"
fi
kv_nonprod_replay_status=$(vault_confirm_path "kv/nonprod/saml/replay/redis")
kv_prod_replay_status=$(vault_confirm_path "kv/prod/saml/replay/redis")

# Output the minimal paste block
echo "Minimal paste block"
echo "- Jira"
echo "  - Sprint IDs"
# Default expected names: SAML Hardening Sprint 1..4
for i in 1 2 3 4; do
  id_line=$(printf "%s\n" "${sprint_lines[@]}" | awk -F': ' -v n="SAML Hardening Sprint ${i}" '$1==n{print $2}' | head -n1)
  if [[ -n "$id_line" ]]; then
    echo "    - SAML Hardening Sprint ${i}: ${id_line}"
  else
    echo "    - SAML Hardening Sprint ${i}: <SPRINT_ID_${i}>"
  fi
done
echo "  - Custom field IDs"
echo "    - Environment: ${env_id:-<customfield_#####>}"
echo "    - Risk: ${risk_id:-<customfield_#####>}"
echo "    - Tracking OKR: ${okr_id:-<customfield_#####>}"
echo "- GitHub repos"
# security-reviews
sr_branch="${repo_defaults[security-reviews]:-main}"
echo "  - ${GITHUB_ORG}/security-reviews: ${GITHUB_ORG}/security-reviews${sr_branch:+ (default branch: ${sr_branch})}"
# auth-service
as_branch="${repo_defaults[auth-service]:-main}"
echo "  - ${GITHUB_ORG}/auth-service: ${GITHUB_ORG}/auth-service${as_branch:+ (default branch: ${as_branch})}"
# admin-ui
ui_branch="${repo_defaults[admin-ui]:-main}"
echo "  - ${GITHUB_ORG}/admin-ui: ${GITHUB_ORG}/admin-ui${ui_branch:+ (default branch: ${ui_branch})}"
# infra / infra-terraform
if [[ -n "$infra_path" ]]; then
  echo "  - ${infra_path%%:*}: ${infra_path%:*} (confirm ${infra_path#*:} path)"
else
  # Fallback: show candidates
  for c in $INFRA_CANDIDATES; do
    echo "  - ${GITHUB_ORG}/${c} or ${GITHUB_ORG}/${c}: ${GITHUB_ORG}/${c} (confirm /terraform/modules path)"
  done
fi
# qa-automation
qa_branch="${repo_defaults[qa-automation]:-main}"
echo "  - ${GITHUB_ORG}/qa-automation: ${GITHUB_ORG}/qa-automation${qa_branch:+ (default branch: ${qa_branch})}"
echo "- Slack"
echo "  - #auth-alerts: ${auth_alerts_id:-<CXXXXXXXX>}"
echo "  - #oncall-sre: ${oncall_sre_id:-<CXXXXXXXX>}"
echo "- PagerDuty"
echo "  - auth-service: ${pd_auth_service:-<PD_SERVICE_OR_ESC_ID>}"
echo "  - edge/gateway: ${pd_edge_gateway:-<PD_SERVICE_OR_ESC_ID>}"
echo "  - redis/cache: ${pd_redis_cache:-<PD_SERVICE_OR_ESC_ID>}"
echo "- Vault and CI"
echo "  - kv/nonprod/saml/metadata/{tenant}: ${kv_nonprod_meta_status:-<CONFIRM>}"
echo "  - kv/prod/saml/metadata/{tenant}: ${kv_prod_meta_status:-<CONFIRM>}"
echo "  - kv/nonprod/saml/replay/redis: ${kv_nonprod_replay_status:-<CONFIRM>}"
echo "  - kv/prod/saml/replay/redis: ${kv_prod_replay_status:-<CONFIRM>}"
echo "  - GitHub OIDC role: saml-hardening-ro"
echo "  - GitHub OIDC auth path: auth/jwt/role/saml-hardening-ro"
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

- It’s a single piece of spring steel plus two removable wire handles—cheap, strong, endlessly reusable.
- The geometry does a lot: wide mouth, concentrated clamping force, flat back so stacks stay neat.
- Hidden affordances: fold the handles down to lock, pop one off to mount as a hook, or use them as cable guides, toothpaste squeezers, phone stands. It’s modularity without moving parts.
- It telegraphs how to use it. No manual, no language.

Infuriating: shower temperature controls
- No standard: clockwise for hot here, counterclockwise there; push-pull for flow in some places, single lever in others.
- No feedback: you adjust “warmth” by guesswork, with a two‑second delay and scald risk. Hotels turn this into a mini‑boss fight.
- Fixes are simple: show target temperature in degrees, add a physical detent at safe-warm, separate flow from mix, and preserve last setting. A cheap thermostatic cartridge plus a clear scale would save water, time, and yelps.

Runner‑up gripe: microwave interfaces
- We mostly use 3 buttons: add 30 seconds, power level, start. Yet many have dozens of cryptic presets. A big “Start +30s” button, a knob for time, and a clear power slider would cover 99% of use.

Your turn: what’s a humble object you think nails (or fumbles) its design?

turns.speaker: A
turns.content_clean:
Nails it: the Bic Cristal pen
- One-piece hex barrel prevents rolling, gives grip, and is cheap to mold. Clear body shows ink level—feedback at a glance.
- Tiny vent hole equalizes pressure so it writes more consistently and reduces leaks on planes.
- The cap clicks on both ends, adds a pocket clip, and has an airway for safety. The nub on the cap keeps it from fully sealing—smart failure mode.
- The tungsten-carbide ball is durable; the line is predictable on almost any paper. No learning curve, works when abused, costs cents.

Fumbles it: stovetop burner controls
- Knob-to-burner mapping is often ambiguous; front-left knob sometimes drives back-left burner. You look, guess, then touch a hot pan to check.
- No meaningful “temperature.” Numbers 1–10 are arbitrary; simmer is a hunt, not a setting.
- Weak feedback: tiny indicator lights, no per-burner timers, no memory of last level.
- Fixes: mirror the cooktop layout around the knobs; illuminate the active burner outline; use numeric power with a tactile detent at “simmer;” add per-burner timers and last-setting recall. On induction, detect a pan and auto-cut if removed. A little mapping and feedback would save food and fingers.

Got another everyday object you love or love to hate?

turns.speaker: A
turns.content_clean:
Nails it: the humble binder clip
- Triangular spring steel gives huge mechanical advantage; grips hard without tearing. Flat jaws spread force, so pages stay neat.
- Flip-up handles are multipurpose: lever to open, or fold down to lock; remove to make it ultra-low profile; use as a hook or cable guide.
- Sizes map intuitively to stack thickness; you “try one up” and it just works. Reusable forever, costs pennies, failure is graceful (it pops off instead of chewing paper).

Fumbles it: microwave oven controls
- Inconsistent flows: some want Power → Time → Start; others Start is also +30s; many bury basics behind “Menu” codes. You shouldn’t need a manual to heat soup.
- Power levels are opaque. “50%” means duty cycle, not half the wattage continuously; defrost is a black box, often half-thawing, half-cooking.
- Feedback is weak. Tiny displays, beep spam with no mute, no visible stage programming, and turntable toggles hidden in hieroglyphic icons.
- Fixes: one obvious flow (dial or +/- for time, big Start/+30s, big Stop/Reset). Label power in watts and duty cycle, with plain-language presets (Melt butter 20% duty, 200 W). Show stages on-screen and let you edit. Dedicated mute toggle. Simple defrost by weight with a probe option and mid-cycle prompt. Memory for last program, knob with tactile detents for quick adjustments mid-run.

Want to pick another? Hotel shower controls, door handles vs. knobs, or TV remotes are ripe for love/hate.

turns.speaker: A
turns.content_clean:
Love/hate, round 2. Here are three:

Hotel shower controls
- Nails it:
  - Single‑lever thermostatic mixer with a numeric temp scale and a separate flow control. You set temperature once; it remembers.
  - Big, tactile diverter with obvious icons (tub, handheld, rain) and hard detents you can feel with wet hands.
  - Anti‑scald/pressure‑balancing valve, warm‑up pause, and controls reachable from outside the spray.
  - Subtle feedback: a color ring or small display that shows target temp and “heating” vs “ready.”
- Fumbles it:
  - Two-handle guessing games, reversed hot/cold, or unlabeled mixers with no temp memory.
  - Hidden diverters (pull the tub spout? tiny knob behind the head?), slippery chrome nubs, stiff cartridges.
  - Touch panels with lag, no feedback, or hotel-specific mystery icons; rain-only heads with weak pressure.
- Fixes:
  - Standardize: thermostatic mixer, 38–40°C default with a safe override button; separate on/off from temp.
  - Clear ISO icons, large-text temp scale, diverter with tactile positions and labeling at eye level.
  - Warm‑up pause, mid‑cycle temp nudge without re-diverting, and a simple one-tile “How to use” graphic.

Door handles vs. knobs
- Nails it:
  - Lever handles (ADA-friendly) with return-to-door to avoid snagging; clear push plates on push side, pulls on pull side.
  - Beveled latch that self-aligns; privacy indicator you can see from a distance; panic bars for exits.
  - Visual affordances: vertical pull = pull; flat plate = push; asymmetric shapes that imply action.
- Fumbles it:
  - Round knobs (slippery, hard for arthritis), identical hardware both sides causing push/pull confusion.
  - Fake knobs on push doors; mirrored glass with hidden edges; levers oriented the wrong way.
  - Misaligned strikes so you need shoulder bumps; handles that catch sleeves or bags.
- Fixes:
  - Default to levers; use plates on push side, D-shaped pulls on pull side; consistent height and hand clearance.
  - Tactile cues or arrows on the lever tip; clear “PUSH/PULL” where architecture is ambiguous.
  - Soft-close, reliable auto-latching; hold-open options for carts; obvious occupancy and egress cues.

TV remotes
- Nails it:
  - Core-only layout: power, input, volume/mute, channel, D‑pad/select, back/home, transport cluster, numeric pad optional.
  - Backlit, sculpted keys with distinct shapes for blind operation; RF/Bluetooth plus IR blaster for legacy gear.
  - Find‑my‑remote beeper, rechargeable (USB‑C or cradle), and user-mappable shortcut buttons.
  - Sensible skips (±10s, ±30s) and a consistent long‑press/short‑press language.
- Fumbles it:
  - 60-button clutter, tiny labels, cryptic color keys, old “mode” sliders (TV/Cable/DVD) that strand users.
  - Line‑of‑sight IR only; Input cycles that loop past the target; unchangeable app keys you always hit by accident.
  - No backlight, no tactile differentiation; batteries that corrode in seldom-used rooms.
- Fixes:
  - Cap the button count and group by task with spacing and shape variance; automatic or tap-to-wake backlight.
  - Universal control via HDMI‑CEC with clear on‑screen prompts for input switching.
  - User-configurable app buttons; optional voice with push‑to‑talk and a privacy slider.
  - Rechargeable power with a base that also pings the remote; on‑screen overlays that label soft keys.

Want to do one more? Elevator panels, office chairs, or stovetop burners (knob-to-burner mapping!) are excellent UX case studies.

turns.speaker: A
turns.content_clean:
Stovetop burners (knob-to-burner mapping!)
- Nails it:
  - 1:1 mapping: a 2x2 knob cluster laid out like the burners; off at 12 o’clock with clear index marks you can see and feel.
  - Per‑burner LEDs right by each knob and residual‑heat indicators near each zone; color ring that brightens with power, shifts to red when hot.
  - Front/side‑mounted controls out of the heat plume; fine low‑end control with smooth taper and tactile detents for simmer.
  - Induction: pan detection, auto‑sizing, bridge zones, per‑zone timers with auto‑off; child lock; gentle but distinct haptics/tones.
  - Gas: one‑handed ignition, auto‑reignite and flame‑failure cutoff, sturdy continuous grates, high‑contrast flame visibility.

- Fumbles it:
  - Inline row of identical knobs with a tiny, confusing map; reversed or ambiguous burner pairing; “off” indistinguishable from low.
  - Touch‑only controls with lag, no haptic feedback, shared “hot surface” light for all burners, or long‑press rituals to start.
  - Strongest burners stuck at the back; controls behind pots; wobbly pans; hard‑to‑clean crevices that trap spills.
  - Gas without safety shutoff; induction that times out mid‑stir; alerts that sound like the timer or are inaudible under a hood.

- Fixes:
  - Map isomorphically: arrange knobs to mirror burner layout (and print the map next to them); use large, high‑contrast markings and an off detent bump.
  - Distinguish zones: subtle texture/shape variance per knob; illuminated ring per burner that tracks level and pulses when a timer ends.
  - Separate power from level: press to toggle on/off (returns to zero), rotate for heat; allow quick “boost” and precise ± nudges.
  - For touch cooktops: put a vertical slider next to each zone with haptic click; direct 0–9 or temperature entry; gesture to swap pans between linked zones.
  - Safety first: flame‑failure + auto‑reignite (gas); pan‑absence + boil‑over pause + auto‑shutoff (induction); child lock; clear residual‑heat by zone.
  - Ergonomics: controls forward/side, shielded; front power burners and stable grates; consistent knob height and knuckle clearance.
  - Clarity: simple “How to use” tile under the lid/inside a drawer; ISO heat/lock icons; audible, distinct tones per event.

Want to tackle elevator panels next? Lots to love/hate around floor logic, door‑close myths, and accessibility.

turns.speaker: A
turns.content_clean:
Love this topic. Elevator UX is a candy store of good intentions, odd myths, and life‑safety constraints. Here’s a stab in the same format.

Elevator panels (hall + car + destination-dispatch)
- Nails it:
  - Clear mapping of calls: separate, big Up/Down hall buttons with illuminated feedback; hall lanterns/arrows with distinct tones (1 chime up, 2 chimes down) and visible from the waiting area.
  - Car panels with large, high‑contrast, backlit buttons; raised numerals plus Braille/tactile to the lower-left of each button; strong, unambiguous “registered” light per floor.
  - Door controls that behave predictably: Door Open reopens immediately and holds while pressed or via a Door Hold function; Door Close works in service/attendant/fire modes and gives feedback when active.
  - Position/Direction indicators that are legible at a glance: dot‑matrix or LCD with big arrows; floor labels that match building wayfinding (G, L, M, P1–P5, 1–12, 14…).
  - Announcements: spoken floor numbers and travel direction; distinct arrival chimes per direction; announced door actions (“Doors opening/closing”).
  - Accessibility: panel height within reach range; bottom row reachable from seated position; beveled edges to avoid knuckle scrape; non-slip, well-lit thresholds; full-height light curtains for door protection.
  - Errors handled gracefully: overload signal with clear message; call-cancel button or long-press to unselect; intercom with two-way audio and location auto-sent; emergency stop only where code allows and with recoverable guidance.
  - Destination dispatch done right: kiosks at natural approach points; big physical keys or responsive touch; immediate assignment with car letter + arrow + auditory cue; the same car letter repeats on jamb lantern and inside the car.
  - Consistency and speed: snappy button response (<100 ms); visible dwell countdown; fair queueing during peaks with clear “Car A for 7–12” grouping.

- Fumbles it:
  - Tiny, glossy, low-contrast buttons in a vertical wall of sameness; “13” missing without explanation; parking/mezzanine unlabeled or cryptic.
  - Door Close placebo: button lights but is ignored in normal mode with no indication; or Door Open that times out aggressively, pinching traffic.
  - Destination dispatch that hides floors behind pages, assigns silently, or reassigns after you’ve committed; kiosks after the turnstiles with nowhere to queue.
  - Hall lanterns that are small, off-axis, or arrive with the car (too late); inaudible chimes under lobby noise.
  - No correction path: mis-pressed floors can’t be deselected; cancel clears all riders’ selections.
  - Accessibility misses: Braille placed on the button instead of adjacent; too-small raised text; panels mounted too high; reflective finishes; announcements too fast or absent.
  - Safety UX gaps: weak door protection (two-beam sensors only); harsh nudge mode without clear warning; ambiguous emergency controls; alarm indistinguishable from arrival chime.
  - Confusing floor logic: mixed G/1/0 across buildings; sky lobbies with poor signage; shuttle/express cars not called out; rear door openings not indicated on the panel.

- Fixes:
  - Make calls obvious:
    - Big, high-contrast Up/Down hall buttons with strong tactile click and bright ring light; mount where people naturally wait.
    - Lanterns/arrows above/beside doors, visible from 20+ feet; 1 chime for up, 2 for down; repeat arrow and chime at the jamb.
  - Legible, touchable car panels:
    - 20–30 mm diameter buttons, 2–3 mm travel, clear detent; 70%+ contrast; anti-glare finish; per-press light with immediate feedback.
    - Raised numerals and Braille at consistent locations; add large text for G, M, P1–P5; provide an on-panel floor legend if numbering is nonstandard.
    - Put frequently used floors (Lobby, Parking) as large dedicated keys at the bottom row; group floors logically; include Rear Door indicator.
  - Door behavior clarity:
    - Door Open: holds while pressed and via a timed Door Hold key with visible countdown (and supervisor timeout).
    - Door Close: label with an info icon; when disabled, pressing shows a “Door Close not available” blink/voice so it’s not a mystery. When enabled (attendant/service), light solid and accelerate close.
    - Aggressive nudge only with pre-tone and spoken warning; never remove the light curtain—use full-height curtains and gentle re-close.
  - Destination dispatch UX:
    - Kiosks before turnstiles with space to queue; one-hand, glove-friendly buttons or low-latency touch; numeric keypad plus common-floor shortcuts; accessibility mode with audio prompts and haptic.
    - Immediate, persistent assignment: big letter, arrow, and nearest door; repeat the letter at the door jamb and inside the car; don’t reassign unless you miss the car.
    - Group riders transparently: show “Car C: 6, 7, 8”; allow correction with a Cancel/Change button that reissues an assignment without starting over.
  - Feedback everywhere:
    - Exterior: next-car ETA or “Serving floors 15–30” during peak; interior: next stop and remaining stops list; soft illumination pulses at arrival.
    - Voice: clear, slow, localizable announcements with volume that rides ambient noise; language toggle where relevant.
  - Accessibility and ergonomics:
    - Panel height: top row ~48–54 in, lowest row ~34–40 in; angled panel to face rider; consistent spacing; knuckle clearance around edges.
    - Tactile arrow on Door Open/Close; textured edge or color ring around Alarm and Intercom; distinct shapes for critical buttons.
    - Handrail placement that doesn’t block panel; space for mobility devices; floor braille at threshold; tactile wayfinding from lobby.
  - Error handling and safety:
    - Overload: clear tone + “Car overloaded—please exit” voice; show current capacity.
    - Stuck/mislevel: lock doors, announce, dispatch help via auto-dial; keep riders informed with periodic updates.
    - Fire/service modes: hide or guard advanced controls; provide “In Fire Service” explanation tile; ensure firefighters’ panel is discrete and unambiguous.
  - Wayfinding and floor logic:
    - Standardize labels with building signage; show a simple “You are here; these cars serve floors …” board at each bank.
    - Call out express/sky-lobby logic with diagrams; indicate rear-door openings on the panel and via pre-arrival announcement.
  - Hygiene and durability:
    - Sealed, replaceable switch modules; antimicrobial, matte finishes; drip edges; easy-clean panel glass; vandal-resistant fasteners.
  - Performance and fairness:
    - Snappy inputs; predictive grouping during peaks; visible “Peak Up” mode indicator so waits feel explained; park cars at demand floors off-peak.

Myth busting quick hits
- Door Close: Often disabled in normal public mode to comply with timing and safety; it works in attendant/service/fire modes. Provide clear feedback either way.
- Pressing both Up and Down: Increases dispatcher noise and can slow service. Better: choose your actual direction; system should discourage dual calls visually.
- Destination dispatch “always faster”: It’s faster when paired with good lobby flow and clear assignments; otherwise it feels opaque. Clarity beats raw optimization.

If you want, we can sketch a model panel: button sizes/spacing, lettering, and a kiosk layout for destination dispatch that minimizes missed cars and supports screen reader/haptics.

turns.speaker: A
turns.content_clean:
Love this. You’ve covered 90% of the real-world pain points. A few extra angles to round it out, plus a concrete “model” panel and kiosk spec you can react to.

Gaps and nuances worth adding
- Codes and standards alignment: Design to meet or exceed ADA/ABA/ICC A117.1, EN 81-70, ISO 4190/8100-1, local fire code (ASME A17.1/CSA B44 in NA), and speech intelligibility guidelines (STI ≥ 0.6).
- Cognitive load: Reduce choice paralysis. Use chunking, floor grouping, and “landmark floors” as primary affordances. Prefer physical affordance (key shape, travel) over color alone.
- Security and privacy: Integrate with PACS/turnstiles. Hide restricted floors on the public kiosk; reveal only authorized destinations after credential. Consider “masked destination” mode for VIPs/clinics.
- Hospitals/clinics: Add bed-car features (longer door dwell, stretcher mode), sterile-friendly materials, negative-pressure floors flagged clearly, and “Code Blue” priority inputs with visual quieting.
- Hotels/residential: Badge-unlocks floor, plus a “My Floor” large key after credential. Night mode: lower chime volume, softer door motion profile.
- Double-deck and shuttle/sky-lobby: Make deck letter inseparable from car letter (e.g., C-Upper). Show deck on jamb and in-car indicator. Pre-arrival announce deck + which door(s).
- Earthquake/fire/evac: Include earthquake operation (seismic switch, evacuation landing logic), mass-notification audio override, evac-mode signage that persists after power dips.
- Touchless/assistive: Add hover/proximity activation with confirm-to-commit, QR/NFC call stations, BLE/mobile call with privacy-respecting tokenization. Make the mobile app mirror kiosk UX.
- Cyber and uptime: Kiosk hardening, least-privilege between dispatch and access control, signed firmware, offline degraded modes (falls back to conventional up/down collective if kiosk fails).
- Telemetry and fairness: Monitor call-to-door times by cohort (mobility device users, peak windows), fairness metrics (95th percentile wait), and “panel hit but no boarding” as a confusion signal.

Model hall station and lantern
- Hall call panel:
  - Height: centerline of Up/Down at 42–48 in; bottom edge ≥ 34 in.
  - Buttons: 28–32 mm diameter, 2.2–2.8 mm travel, 0.5–0.7 N actuation, concave cap, matte.
  - Tactile: Raised up/down arrows with ≥ 1 mm relief; Braille below-left of each arrow.
  - Feedback: 100 ms light-on; 2-second soft pulse acknowledge; cancel by long-press (1.5 s) per direction; visual “You pressed Up” text cue where display exists.
- Lantern/arrival:
  - Placement: Above/beside each door and repeated on jamb at eye level (~60–66 in).
  - Visual: 75–100 mm arrows; 300+ cd/m² daytime legibility; wide-angle diffusers.
  - Audio: 1 chime up, 2 down; 1.5–3 kHz content; auto-level to ambient; 55–65 dBA at 1 m (lobby), adjustable.
  - Early notice: Pre-arrival arrow lights ≥ 1.5 s before door open target; don’t debut with the door.

Model car operating panel (COP)
- Panel geometry:
  - Mounting: Bottom row 34–40 in AFF; top row ≤ 54 in AFF. Panel angled 10–15° toward rider if sidewall-mounted.
  - Spacing: 38–45 mm centers; 12–16 mm gap to bezel for knuckle clearance.
- Buttons:
  - Floors: 26–30 mm; 2–3 mm travel; high-contrast legends (≥ 70% LRV contrast). Raised numerals (≥ 1 mm) lower-left of each button; Grade 2 Braille lower-left, not on the cap.
  - Dedicated large keys (32–36 mm): Lobby, Parking, Help/Intercom, Alarm, Door Open/Close, Door Hold. Unique shapes for Alarm (domed) and Help (ringed).
  - Registration: Per-button halo solid when registered; long-press (1.2 s) to deselect own floor; a separate, guarded “Cancel All” behind a confirm (double-tap or hold).
- Copy/labels:
  - Floors mirror building signage exactly (G, L, M, P1–P5, 1–12, 14…); provide small legend panel for nonstandard ranges.
  - Rear door indicator lamp and “Rear door active” pre-arrival voice line.
- Indicators:
  - Direction: Big arrows; next stop text; remaining stops list on small OLED where permitted.
  - Dwell: 3–7 s visible countdown ring around Door Open when held; extendable by Door Hold with displayed seconds remaining.
- Audio:
  - Voice: Floor numbers, direction, door actions. Pace: 140–160 wpm, neutral local accent; ducking on chimes. Bilingual toggle or auto per locale.
  - Tones: Distinct from alarms; pre-nudge tone + “Doors closing” before gentle re-close.
- Safety/assistive:
  - Full-height light curtain; disable harsh nudge; re-open sensitivity high for carts/canes.
  - Intercom: One-press to connect; two-way full-duplex; sends car ID, floor, building to monitoring; text/visual reassurance “Help is on the line.”
  - Tactile arrows on door controls; textured guard ridge around Alarm/Help.
- Service modes:
  - Door Close behaves per mode; if disabled, button gives “Door Close not available” blink + voice. In service/attendant, solid light + faster close profile.

Model destination-dispatch kiosk
- Placement and flow:
  - Before turnstiles with 4–6 ft queuing depth; one kiosk per 2–3 cars; at natural desire lines. Secondary kiosks post-turnstile for corrections.
  - Mount height: 38–48 in to primary input surface; 15–20° tilt; side clearance for wheelchairs.
- Inputs:
  - Physical keypad: 0–9, Back, Enter; 20–25 mm sculpted keys; high contrast; gloved operation.
  - Touch targets: ≥ 12×12 mm; 10 ms scan, <50 ms touch latency; haptics on confirm.
  - Shortcuts: Dedicated large keys for Lobby, Cafeteria, Parking, Sky Lobby. Badge/NFC tap unlocks personalized “My Floors.”
  - Accessibility mode: Long-press “Access” key or hold badge to trigger screen reader, audio prompts over bone-conductive pad or speaker, high-contrast theme, and “single-switch” scanning.
- Output:
  - Assignment card persists 8–12 s: large Car Letter + arrow + nearest door location; repeats on jamb and in-car display. Audible “Car C, to your right.”
  - Group transparency: Show “Car C: 6, 7, 8.” Never reassign after the rider crosses a virtual commitment line, unless the car departs; offer “Change/Cancel” to reissue.
  - Countdown/ETA: Subtle progress bar; don’t induce run-chasing.
- Error/correction:
  - Mis-press: Clear per-digit echo, backspace; on ambiguous entries, propose candidates by building map.
  - Missed car: Detect via sensor/time-out and auto-reissue same car group preference.
- Security:
  - After credential, show only permitted floors; sensitive destinations masked as “Authorized” without explicit labels. Privacy timeout clears screen quickly.

Peak, fairness, and transparency
- Visible mode indicators: “Up Peak,” “Down Peak,” “Lunchtime Peak.” Explain grouping briefly on kiosks; perceived fairness reduces anxiety.
- Allocation goals: Minimize 95th-percentile wait and time-to-destination, not just average. Protect edges: ensure at least one car cycles through low-demand floors periodically off-peak.
- Staging: Park cars at predicted demand floors with soft wake cues; surface “Next car ~25 s” where useful.

Wayfinding integrations
- Bank directory at each lobby: “You are here; these cars serve 16–30.” Simple, persistent, non-scrolling print or e-paper.
- Mixed cores: Color-code banks consistently across signage, kiosks, jamb labels, and in-car indicators.
- Rear/side openings and sky lobbies: Diagrammatic callouts on COP and landings; pre-arrival “Rear doors opening.”

Testing and validation
- Design sprints in-situ: Tape-and-cardboard mockups at actual sightlines; 10–20 user trials per cohort (mobility device users, older adults, non-native speakers).
- Instrumentation: Log button press-to-feedback latency, call-to-door, door dwell extensions, cancel rates, “pressed but didn’t board,” mislevel/stuck incidents, intercom false positives.
- Audio tuning: Set chime/voice SPL against ambient; verify STI ≥ 0.6 in lobbies; verify tonal distinctness from fire alarms.
- Failure drills: Kiosk offline → fall back to hall up/down; car UI survives network blips; fire/service modes display plain-language tiles.

Myth-busting additions
- Holding Door Open “hurts the system”: It lengthens a single stop but can improve overall flow if used at transfer floors. Make dwell extensions visible so riders self-moderate.
- “Close Door makes it faster”: In most public modes, dispatch sets minimum dwell for safety and boarding; shaving 0.5–1.0 s rarely changes trip times more than perception does. Provide feedback to avoid superstition.
- “DD eliminates buttons inside cars”: Keep a minimal in-car panel for redundancy, corrections, and emergency wayfinding; pure-kiosk cars increase brittleness.

If you want, I can sketch a to-scale panel/KP layout with exact dimensions, legends, and state diagrams for:
- Conventional COP with 24 landings + rear door + service strip
- Hall station + lantern + jamb repeaters
- DD kiosk with keypad-first flow, accessibility branch, and miss-recovery
Say how many floors, any rear openings, and whether this is office, hotel, hospital, or mixed-use, and we’ll tune it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.content_clean:
This is an excellent, real-world spec. A few refinements, edge-cases, and checks I’d layer on, plus what I need to produce the to-scale layouts and state diagrams you asked for.

Refinements and gotchas
- Standards nuance
  - Tactile/Braille placement: ICC A117.1/ADA generally expect raised characters to the left of the control, with Braille directly below those characters (not offset). Your “lower-left” is close; I’d align to “left with Braille directly below” to avoid AHJ pushback.
  - Evacuation/firefighter: If using occupant-evacuation elevators (IBC 3008/EN 81-76), reserve signage, power, lobby protection, and controls differ from standard FEO Phase I/II (ASME A17.1/CSA B44, EN 81-72). Make sure the UI clearly distinguishes these modes.
  - Seismic: If EN 81-77 or local seismic rules apply, include car-door relevel logic and “post-seismic inspection mode” indicators in UI.
- Accessibility depth
  - Hearing: Add audio induction loop in cars and at kiosks/intercoms; T-coil icon; certify STI and loop SNR. Provide full-text visual equivalents for all spoken phrases.
  - Vision: Ensure no critical info is color-only; verify luminance contrast (≥70% LRV) under glossy stone lobbies. Avoid PWM flicker in backlights; meet IEC TR 63158 flicker guidance.
  - Cognitive: Hick-Hyman—keep visible choices low; your chunking/landmarks plan is great. Add “recent choices” and “My Floor” large key after credential. Provide “undo” everywhere.
  - Language/scripts: Plan for bilingual or tri-lingual with non-Latin numerals if needed (e.g., Arabic-Indic). Keep floor labels 1:1 with building signage to avoid code-switch errors.
- Security/privacy
  - PACS: Prefer OSDP Secure Channel over legacy Wiegand; least-privilege and explicit timeouts. Masked destinations should never appear in logs visible to attendants.
  - Cyber: Add IEC 62443/UL 2900 posture, secure boot, signed firmware, SBOM, and staged OTA. Separate networks for dispatch vs. PACS; rate-limit and fault-contain kiosk inputs.
  - Shoulder-surfing: Use privacy films on kiosks, quick redaction, and verbal-only assignment replay via bone-conduction pad on request.
  - Mobile: Tokenize credentials; support offline signed, short-lived tokens in case of brief PACS/network loss; explicit consent for analytics per GDPR/CCPA/HIPAA where applicable.
- Hospitals/clinics extras
  - Infection control: Material compatibility with quats/bleach; rounded bezels; gasketed seams (IP54 where appropriate). ICRA planning for retrofits.
  - Code Blue: Priority input should also quiet visual clutter and suppress nonessential prompts; add “staff escort mode” to allow multi-floor sequences without re-badging.
- Hotels/residential
  - Night profiles: Tie chime/SPL and door-motion profiles to quiet hours per property policy; dim indicators to a floor but keep minimum accessibility contrast.
- Double-deck specifics
  - Always speak deck on approach and in-car: “Car C Upper, doors on both sides/right side.” Mirror deck letter on jamb and in-car next-stop.
- Telemetry/fairness
  - Accessibility-aware dispatch: Track mobility-assist cohorts and weight assignment to reduce their 95th-percentile waits. Use “pressed but didn’t board” as a retraining label for UI friction.
  - Transparent modes: Your peak-mode transparency is spot-on—reduces perceived unfairness.
- Hardware/industrial

Somewhere a hinge makes its vowel, and your ribs echo, patient hinges, too.

No trumpet, only the wrist’s red lantern swinging its gentle arc.

Let the sink practice rain

A pencil carries weather low in its graphite,

If a name is barbed in the mouth,

Curtains keep an archive of breezes,
then unlearn each rumor at the lift of your hand.

The bell is a bird with a brass throat;
teach it hello, teach it later.

Keys dream in a dish that loves eclipse,
circling metal moons under the fruit.

Let your coat be cave enough for weather to kneel,
tame in the dark wool near your wrist.

Let the bed be a small ferry with no wake,
carrying even the loose change of sleep.

Let the pillow be coast and harbor,
your breath the buoy counting arrivals.

The moon hems the night with quiet buttons,

Tile whispers syllables of cool, heel and arch learning fluency.

If silence takes your name apart,
hum with all the vowels you have left.

If memory fogs the mirror,
print forgiveness in one knuckle, rinse the day clear.

If hunger requests proof,
offer steam and plural spoons, the evidence of heat.

you sign anew in paperclips and elastic.

Some hinge makes its one wide vowel,
and your ribs answer, patient doors.

and drops no stitch in the dark’s sweater.

No trumpet, only the lantern in your pulse,
swinging a red arc between room and room.
